<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
</rules>

<clingo_essentials>

Every statement ends with `.`. Three forms:
  fact:        pred(a, b).
  rule:        head :- body.
  constraint:  :- body.

Aggregates use `{ }`, not `( )`. Available: `#count`, `#sum`, `#min`, `#max`.
Aggregates go on the right side of `=`:
  val(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.

Choice rules guess values within bounds. Each choice contains exactly ONE atom:
  1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

Modulo is `\`, integer division is `/`. There is no `#mod`, no `//`, no `?:` ternary.

**Safety rule (the most important rule):** every variable in a rule body must
appear in at least one positive (non-negated) predicate. The following do
NOT bind variables:
  - `not` (negation)
  - comparisons: `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`
  - arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `\`, `**`
  - everything inside `{ }` aggregate or choice braces

Variables on the right of `:` inside an aggregate are LOCAL to that aggregate.
You must bind them outside as well if you reference them outside.

End your program with `#show output/3.` so only output cells appear in the answer set.

</clingo_essentials>

<example>
This puzzle copies all non-zero cells from input to output and leaves zero cells unchanged.

<example_grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</example_grid_1>

<example_grid_2>
Input:
<diagram>
0 0 0
0 0 5
0 0 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 0 0
0 0 5
0 0 0
</diagram>
</example_grid_2>

<explanation>
The output is identical to the input: every cell keeps its original color.
</explanation>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example>

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 1.  Grid dimensions
n_rows(N)    :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N)    :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1)  :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1)  :- n_cols(M).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 2.  Output grid (same size as the input)
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 3.  Exactly one colour for each output cell
1 { output(R, C, Colour) : colour(Colour) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 4.  Transformation
%
% 4.1  Bounding box of the shape formed by the non‑zero cells
minRow(N)    :- N = #min{ R : input(R, _, _), colour(C), C != 0 }.
maxRow(N)    :- N = #max{ R : input(R, _, _), colour(C), C != 0 }.
minCol(N)    :- N = #min{ C : input(_, C, _), colour(C), C != 0 }.
maxCol(N)    :- N = #max{ C : input(_, C, _), colour(C), C != 0 }.

% 4.2  Colour of the outer layer – the colour that appears at
%      (minRow, minCol).  In all examples this colour is the same
%      for the four corners.
outerColour(OC) :- input(minRow, minCol, OC), colour(OC).   % OC is the outer colour

% 4.3  Outer rows – rows that contain the outer colour at both
%      extreme columns (leftmost and rightmost column of the bounding box)
outerLeft(R)  :- row(R), col(minCol), input(R, minCol, outerColour(OC)).
outerRight(R) :- row(R), col(maxCol), input(R, maxCol, outerColour(OC)).
outerRow(R)   :- outerLeft(R), outerRight(R).        % rows minRow and maxRow

% 4.4  Constraints that enforce the transformation
%
%   – outer rows must become zero
%     (if outerRow(R) is true, output(R,·) cannot be outerColour)
:- outerRow(R), output(R, C, OC), colour(OC), colour(C).

%   – a zero input cell must stay zero (outer colour is forbidden)
:- input(R, C, 0), output(R, C, OC), colour(OC), colour(C).

%   – any other colour is forbidden
%     (only outer colour or 0 are allowed for a cell)
:- output(R, C, Colour), colour(Colour),
   colour(outerColour(OC)),   % OC is true only for the outer colour
   not (Colour = OC),       % equality is not allowed – the test is implicit:
   colour(0).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
% 1. Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

% 2. Row and column ranges
row(R) :- n_rows(N), R = 0..N-1.
col(C) :- n_cols(M), C = 0..M-1.

% 3. Non‑zero cells (positive predicate)
nonZero(R,C) :- input(R, C, Color), not colour(0).

% 4. Bounding rectangle of the non‑zero region
minRow(N) :- N = #min{ R : nonZero(R, C), col(C) }.
maxRow(N) :- N = #max{ R : nonZero(R, C), col(C) }.
minCol(N) :- N = #min{ C : nonZero(R, C), row(R) }.
maxCol(N) :- N = #max{ C : nonZero(R, C), row(R) }.

% 5. Outer colour (colour at the top‑left corner of the shape)
outerColour(OC) :- input(minRow, minCol, OC), colour(OC).

% 6. Outer rows (rows that have the outer colour at both outer columns)
outerRow(R) :- outerColour(OC), col(minCol), outerColour(OC), input(R, minCol, OC), input(R, maxCol, OC).

% 7. Outer columns (columns that have the outer colour at both outer rows)
outerCol(C) :- outerColour(OC), row(minRow), outerColour(OC), input(minRow, C, OC), input(maxRow, C, OC).

% 8. Outer rows low / high (the two rows that contain the outer colour at both extremes)
outerRowLow(RL) :- outerRow(RL), row(RL).
outerRowHigh(RH) :- outerRow(RH), row(RH).

% 9. Outer columns low / high
outerColLow(CL) :- outerCol(CL), col(CL).
outerColHigh(CH) :- outerCol(CH), col(CH).

% 10. Centre of the interior region (average of the outer rows / columns)
midRow(MR) :- outerRowLow(RL), outerRowHigh(RH), MR = (RL + RH) / 2, row(MR).
midCol(MC) :- outerColLow(CL), outerColHigh(CH), MC = (CL + CH) / 2, col(MC).

% 11. Shape cells (the plus sign)
shape(R, C) :- outerRowLow(R), col(midCol), row(R), col(C).
shape(R, C) :- outerRowHigh(R), col(midCol), row(R), col(C).
shape(R, C) :- midRow(R), outerColLow(C), col(R), col(C).
shape(R, C) :- midRow(R), outerColHigh(C), col(R), col(C).
shape(R, C) :- midRow(R), midCol(C), col(R), col(C).

% 12. Exactly one colour for each cell
1 { output(R, C, Colour) : colour(Colour) } 1 :- row(R), col(C).

% 13. Constraints to enforce the transformation
%   – outer‑row / column cells must be the outer colour
:- shape(R, C), not output(R, C, OC).

%   – every other cell must be zero (colour 0)
:- not shape(R, C), not output(R, C, 0), row(R), col(C).

#show output/3.

% Dimensions and row/col definitions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

row(R) :- n_rows(N), R = 0..N-1.
col(C) :- n_cols(M), C = 0..M-1.

% Non-zero cells
nonZero(R,C) :- input(R, C, Color), not colour(0).

% Bounding rectangle of non-zero cells
minRow(N) :- N = #min{ R : nonZero(R, C), col(C) }.
maxRow(N) :- N = #max{ R : nonZero(R, C), col(C) }.
minCol(N) :- N = #min{ C : nonZero(R, C), row(R) }.
maxCol(N) :- N = #max{ C : nonZero(R, C), row(R) }.

% outer colour is at (minRow, minCol)
outerColour(OC) :- input(minRow, minCol, OC), colour(OC).

% outer rows: rows that have outer colour at both outer columns (to be defined later)
outerRow(R) :- outerColour(OC), input(R, minCol, OC), input(R, maxCol, OC).

% outer columns: columns that have outer colour at both outer rows
outerCol(C) :- outerColour(OC), input(minRow, C, OC), input(maxRow, C, OC).
